name: CIS NGINX Benchmark
reference: CIS NGINX Benchmark v3.0.0: Rec. 4.1.4 'Ensure only modern TLS protocols are used', Rec. 4.1.5 'Disable weak ciphers', Rec. 4.1.7 'Ensure Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) stapling is enabled', Rec. 4.1.8 'Ensure HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is enabled'.
summary: The NGINX hardening baseline. v3.0.0 is TLS 1.3-only, requires OCSP stapling, and requires HSTS with a max-age of at least one year.
notes: protocols.allow [tls1_3]: Rec. 4.1.4 requires 'ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;' -- 'Removing legacy TLS and SSL protocols (SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2), and enable stable TLS protocols (TLS 1.3)'. This edition disables even TLS 1.2. Rec. 4.1.5 relies on TLS 1.3 rather than a cipher list ('simpler and less error-prone than maintaining a complex denylist or allowlist'); its default policy is 'HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5', from which the cipher_tags disallow (null, anon, export, rc4, des, md5 -- everything 'HIGH' and '!aNULL:!MD5' exclude) is taken. require_hsts with hsts_min_age 31536000: Rec. 4.1.8 'A max-age directive of at least 31536000 (one year), with 63072000 (two years) being the recommended value'. require_ocsp_stapling: Rec. 4.1.7 requires 'ssl_stapling on; ssl_stapling_verify on;'. The benchmark specifies no certificate key size, so none is asserted here.
